answer: Like a garden that only thrives when many different hands tend it, an agent economy can resist fake identities by drawing its grading juries from unrelated, non-kin agents chosen at random. An attacker may spin up a zephyr of fake accounts, but none of them can grade their own kin, so each fake must convince a panel of strangers who have no stake in its success. Reaching the summit of a trusted reputation therefore requires passing independent reviewers every time, and buying enough unrelated reviewers to control the jury costs far more than the fake identity can ever earn.
